Privacy Policy

Effective date: 15 October 2026. Last updated: 15 October 2026.

This policy explains what the YouTube channel analysis service at ytvideoanalysis.studio (the "service") collects, why, who we share it with, and the choices you have. If anything is unclear, email us at kamalakshya75531@gmail.com.

The short version

  • We collect your account details, or the details Google shares when you sign in with Google.
  • We fetch public YouTube data about the channels you choose to analyse.
  • We use this information only to run the service and keep it secure.
  • We do not sell your personal data, and we do not use it for advertising.
  • You can ask us for a copy of your data, or ask us to correct or delete it.

1. Who we are

The service is run by Kamalakshya Behera, based in India ("we", "us"). We decide how your personal data is used, so we are responsible for it. Some laws call this the "data controller" or "data fiduciary".

Email Kamalakshya75531@gmail.com with any privacy question, request or complaint.

2. What we collect

2.1 Information you give us

  • If you sign up with email and password: your email address, a display name, and your password. If you leave the display name blank, we use the part of your email address before the "@".
  • Your password: we never store your password itself. We store only a scrambled version of it (a bcrypt hash), which cannot be turned back into your password.
  • The channels you analyse: the YouTube channel IDs or @handles you type in, and the options you pick, such as how many videos to scan.
  • Messages: anything you send us by email.

2.2 Information from Google sign-in

If you choose "Continue with Google", Neon Auth handles the sign-in for us. Neon Auth is a service from Neon, our database provider. Google asks you to approve sharing your basic profile. It then sends Neon Auth your Google account ID, name, email address and profile picture. These are the "openid", "email" and "profile" permissions.

Our app then takes only:

  • your name,
  • your email address,
  • whether Google has verified your email address, and
  • an account ID from Neon Auth.

We do not use or store your profile picture. We never see your Google password. We do not use your Google sign-in to access your YouTube account, Gmail, contacts or files.

2.3 Public data from YouTube

When you analyse a channel, the service uses YouTube API Services (the YouTube Data API) with our own API key. It fetches public data only:

  • Channel details: name, description, creation date, subscriber count, view count, video count and the link to the channel image.
  • Up to 50 recent videos: title, description, publish date, and the view, like, comment and favourite counts.
  • On the Comment Sentiment page, only when you click "Analyze comments": up to 30 public top-level comments from each video you choose (up to 20 videos). For each comment we get the commenter's display name, the comment text, its like count and its date.

This information is public on YouTube, but it can include personal data about YouTube creators and commenters. We do not access private YouTube data.

2.4 Information collected automatically

  • Cookies: see section 6.
  • Session records: when you sign in, we save a record of your session in our database. It contains a fingerprint (hash) of your session token, your account ID, your email address, your display name, and when the session started, expires and was ended.
  • Account activity: when your account was created and when you last signed in.
  • Failed sign-in attempts: we count failed sign-in attempts for each email address to slow down password guessing. The count is kept only in our server's memory, not in the database.
  • Server logs: our web server records standard details about each request. These are your IP address, the date and time, the page requested, the page you came from, and your browser type. Our app also writes error logs. The app's code does not write passwords, session tokens or email addresses to these logs.

5. Google user data and YouTube API Services

  • This service uses YouTube API Services. By using the service, you agree to be bound by the YouTube Terms of Service.
  • Google's handling of your data is explained in the Google Privacy Policy.
  • Google user data we receive: through Neon Auth, using the openid, email and profile permissions, we receive your name, email address, whether Google has verified it, and an account ID. See section 2.2.
  • How we use it: only to sign you in and run your account. That means showing your name and email in the app, keeping you signed in, and stopping duplicate accounts.
  • Limited Use: we do not use Google user data for advertising. We do not sell it. We do not share it with anyone, except as needed to provide the service (the providers in section 4) or when the law requires it. Our use and transfer of information received from Google APIs will follow the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
  • Removing access: you can remove this service's access to your Google account at any time in your Google account security settings. This stops future Google sign-ins. To delete what we already hold, email us (see section 7).

6. Cookies

We use only the cookies needed to sign you in and keep the service secure. Without them you cannot sign in, so there is no option to turn them off.

Cookies set on ytvideoanalysis.studio
NameSet byPurposeHow long it lasts
yt_sessionUsKeeps you signed in. It holds a long random code that is linked to your session record.7 days, or until you sign out
yt_oauth_nonceUsUsed only during Google sign-in. It checks that the sign-in finishes in the same browser that started it.10 minutes, and removed when the sign-in finishes
_streamlit_xsrfStreamlit, the framework our app is built withA security cookie that helps block forged requests from other websitesUntil you close your browser

On our HTTPS site, the two cookies we set ourselves (yt_session and yt_oauth_nonce) are sent only over encrypted connections. They are also not sent with most requests that come from other websites (the "SameSite=Lax" setting).

We do not use advertising cookies or analytics trackers. Streamlit has an optional usage-statistics feature. That feature would set an ajs_anonymous_id cookie and send anonymous usage data to Streamlit. We keep it switched off.

Your light or dark theme choice is kept in the page address (for example ?theme=dark), not in a cookie.

When you use Google sign-in, Google and Neon Auth may set their own cookies on their own websites. Their privacy policies apply to those cookies.

How to get a copy of your data, correct it or delete it

There is no delete button in the app yet. Email: kamalakshya75531@gmail.com from the email address on your account. Tell us whether you want a copy of your data, a correction, or deletion of your account. We may ask you to confirm that the request comes from you. We will reply within 30 days.

When we delete your account, we delete your account record and your session records. If you signed in with Google, we also delete the Neon Auth record of your sign-in. Deleted data may stay in our database provider's backups for a short time until those backups are replaced.

If you are a YouTube creator or commenter and want data about your channel or comments removed from our database, email us too.

8. How we protect your data

  • The site uses HTTPS, and plain HTTP addresses redirect to HTTPS.
  • Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes. A password must be at least 10 characters long, and very common passwords are refused.
  • After 5 failed sign-in attempts for an email address, sign-in for that address is paused for 15 minutes.
  • Your session cookie holds a long random code. Our database stores only a fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) of it, not the code itself.
  • Sessions end after 7 days or when you sign out. They are checked against the database at least once a minute, so signing out in one tab ends the others.
  • Google sign-in uses a one-time code. It must finish in the same browser that started it, and only email addresses that Google has verified are accepted. The Neon Auth session is ended straight away, so only our own session is kept.
  • Our app connects to the database over an encrypted connection.

No system is completely secure. If a data breach affects your personal data, we will tell you and the authorities where the law requires it.

9. Where your data is processed

Our web server (on AWS) and our database (on Neon) are in Singapore. Google and Cloudflare run worldwide networks and may process data in other countries. Your data may therefore be processed outside the country where you live, where data protection laws can be different. Where the law requires extra safeguards for these transfers, we rely on the safeguards these providers offer.

10. Your rights

Depending on where you live, data protection laws may give you rights over your personal data. Examples are the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. These rights can include the right to:

  • get a copy of your personal data,
  • correct data that is wrong or out of date,
  • have your data deleted,
  • receive your data in a format you can reuse,
  • object to or limit some uses of your data,
  • withdraw consent where we rely on it, for example by removing our access to your Google account (section 5),
  • name another person to use your rights if you die or cannot act yourself, where the law allows this, and
  • complain to a data protection authority. In the EU or UK, that is your local data protection authority. In India, it is the Data Protection Board of India.

To use any of these rights, email: kamalakshya75531@gmail.com. Please contact us first so we can try to fix the problem. Using your rights is free, and we will not treat you differently for using them.

11. Children

The service is not for anyone under 18, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If you think a child has given us personal data, email: kamalakshya75531@gmail.com and we will delete it.

12. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy. When we do, we will post the new version on this page and change the "Last updated" date at the top. If a change is significant, we will also show a notice in the app before it takes effect.
